_roden_faqs.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Darien?
_roden_faqs.answer: Darien is in McIntosh County, Georgia, so the statute of limitations for most personal injury claims is 2 years from the date of the injury under O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33. Workers' compensation claims have shorter deadlines — you must report within 30 days and file a formal claim within 1 year. Medical malpractice cases follow a discovery rule but have a 5-year outer limit. Missing any of these deadlines will likely bar your claim entirely, so contact our Darien office at (912) 303-5850 as soon as possible to protect your rights.

_roden_faqs.question: What is Georgia's comparative fault law and how does it affect my Darien injury case?
_roden_faqs.answer: Georgia uses a modified comparative fault system under O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33. You can recover damages as long as you are less than 50% responsible for your accident, but your compensation is reduced by your share of fault. For example, if you are found 25% at fault and your total damages are $200,000, you would receive $150,000. If you are 50% or more at fault, you recover nothing. Insurance adjusters often try to assign blame to victims to minimize payouts — our Darien attorneys know how to counter these tactics and protect your right to fair compensation.
